content: Cefotaxime is an antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is also administered before and during certain surgeries to prevent infections. This medication belongs to the cephalosporin class of antibiotics. Administration: Cefotaxime is given by injection into a muscle or vein as directed by a healthcare provider. Before use, inspect the solution for particles or discoloration; do not use it if either is present. For optimal effectiveness, administer the medication at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Dosage: For infants under 3 months old: Safety and efficacy have not been established. For infants over 3 months old: The recommended dose is 80-160 mg/kg/day intravenously, divided every 4-6 hours. Higher doses may be required for severe infections. For infection prevention during surgery: Administer 30-40 mg/kg 30-60 minutes before surgery, followed by 30-40 mg/kg every 6 hours for 24 hours post-surgery. Side Effects: Common side effects include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Rarely, it may cause nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, or loss of appetite. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or vaginal yeast infections. In rare cases, it can cause a severe intestinal condition (C. difficile-associated diarrhea), which may occur during or after treatment. Serious allergic reactions are rare but require immediate medical attention. Precautions: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to cefotaxime, other cephalosporins, or penicillins. This medication may interfere with live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine) and certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. Cefotaxime passes into breast milk, but no serious safety concerns have been reported in breastfeeding infants. Discuss the benefits of breastfeeding with your doctor while considering the clinical need for cefotaxime. Drug Interactions: Cefotaxime may interact with other medications, altering their effects or increasing the risk of side effects. Notable interactions include: Live bacterial vaccines (e.g., BCG, cholera): Avoid co-administration as antibiotics may reduce vaccine efficacy. Aminoglycosides (e.g., gentamicin, tobramycin): Increased risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity; monitor closely. Probenecid: May increase cefotaxime levels by reducing renal clearance. Bacteriostatic agents (e.g., tetracyclines, erythromycin): May reduce the effectiveness of cefotaxime; use with caution. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Cefotaxime is generally considered safe during pregnancy, with no evidence of fetal risk in controlled studies. Minimal data are available on its effects on breastfed infants, but no serious concerns have been reported. Discuss the risks and benefits with your healthcare provider. Storage: Follow the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for proper storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into drains unless instructed. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Overdose: In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention. In the U.S., contact poison control at 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. Important Notes: This summary does not include all possible information about cefotaxime. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete details tailored to your specific health needs.
